headline: Discussed a drainage pipe at 87 Collins Rd and a Flex Storage Building at 154 East Main Street; no votes were recorded.
summary: Members reviewed two wetlands applications on site. One is for a new drainage pipe from Collins Rd to a stream, and the other is for a Flex Storage Building at 154 East Main Street. No votes or other decisions were recorded.
plain_text:
Inland Wetlands & Watercourse Agency 
of The Conservation Commission of the City of Bristol 
Site Walk Meeting of September 16, 2026 
 
 
– 1 – 
 
Application 2076 — Wetlands application for the installation of a new drainage pipe approximately 495' ft. in length 
from Collins Road to a north-west stream at 87 Collins Rd — Lot 51B; Lot 50 — Collins Rd & Lot 147 — Stafford 
Ave; Assessor's Map 53, Lots 50, 51B, and 147; City of Bristol — Department of Public Works, applicant. 
 
Date: Wednesday September 16, 2026 
Application #2076 
Call To Order: 5:00 P.M. 
 
Commission Members: 
• Greg Klimek – Commission Member 
• Faye Duquette – Commission Member 
• Laura Valentino – Commission Member 
• Dave Rooks – Commission Member 
• Justin Bridges- Alternate IWC 
 
Other Attendees: 
• Lukasz Burkacki, Civil Engineer City of Bristol 
• Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works  
 
David Rooks – IWC Chairman: Called the meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.  
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P, E., Director of Public Works: Stated that the public hearing for application #2076, he 
reviewed the site location and the proposed work consisting of replacement of a 12 -inch RCP with a 24-inch pipe 
directed all the way to the top of Coppermine brook. There were no questions asked and no soil borings were 
performed.                  
 
It was also stated that this meeting is not an appropriate time for additional testimony or conversations and that 
commission members are encouraged to write down any questions they may have and ask them during the next 
regularly scheduled meeting of the commission to be held on October 5, 2026.
